LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 LISTENING FOR INFORMATION: INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives, part of Strand 6 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we use different interrogatives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify interrogatives for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use interrogatives appropriately to ask questions for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. take pleasure in using interrogatives in different oral communication contexts.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify interrogatives for comprehension,

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use interrogatives appropriately to ask questions for information,

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. take pleasure in using interrogatives in different oral communication contexts.

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a recorded text on the theme and identify interrogative sentences,

2. read different interrogatives aloud from a wall chart,

3. observe a sample sentence given by the teacher and make own sentences,

4. role play using interrogative sentences and giving responses,

5. collaborate to play a language game involving fishing interrogatives from fashcards,

6. discuss main issues related to the theme using interrogatives.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a recorded text on the theme and identify interrogative sentences,
2. read different interrogatives aloud from a wall chart,
3. observe a sample sentence given by the teacher and make own sentences,
4. role play using interrogative sentences and giving responses,
5. collaborate to play a language game involving fishing interrogatives from fashcards,
6. discuss main issues related to the theme using interrogatives.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Listening for Information: Interrogatives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner creates own sentences during the fishing game and role play.

● Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively when discussing main issues related

to the theme using interrogatives.

Values:
● Love: This is cultivated as the learner respects others when role playing using interrogative sentences and giving

responses.

● Social Justice: This is enhanced as the learner accords each one an equal opportunity when discussing main issues related

to health and diseases.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health issues: These are addressed as the learner interacts with content on health and diseases for information.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to acquire and relate vocabulary acquired from the theme on health and diseases to their learning of similar

concepts in Science and Technology.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify interrogatives for comprehension,
2. use interrogatives appropriately to ask questions for information,
3. take pleasure in using interrogatives in different oral communication contexts.

Remember the key question: How do we use different interrogatives?
